channel.title: Braelyn's Blog
channel.description: Braelyn Boynton on AI and codegen, startups, creative coding, and motorcycle trips around the world.

item.title: Tokyo to Izu, Fuji and the Venus Line
item.description: Four days on a ZX-6R: a Tokyo night ride, the Nishi-Izu Skyline (several times), Mt. Fuji, the Venus Line, and the volcanoes of Shiga Kogen.

item.title: Wittstock
item.description: Soviet-era halls, a gym, a theater and a Lenin statue with something to say, on a lake in northern Brandenburg.

item.title: Fürstenberg
item.description: A giant 1912 flour mill on the edge of a lake, rotting floor by floor. Best sunset of the trip.

item.title: Stop Dooming: Codegen will have its Gang of Four moment
item.description: We're 5.4% through the codegen adoption curve.

item.title: Social Media Trained Our Brains for the Current State of Codegen
item.description: How a decade of social media and algorithmic taste-making primed our brains for the dopamine dynamics of AI code generation tools.

item.title: SF's lack of style: a forcing function
item.description: How San Francisco's lack of fashion culture became a forcing function for authentic self-expression and identity.

item.title: Riding through the UAE
item.description: Dune bashing until 5am, a few hours of sleep, then twelve hours on a Himalayan 450 through the gravel roads and wadis of the Hajar mountains.

item.title: Baja on KLRs
item.description: Four days and about 580 miles around Baja California Sur with Ellie: the East Cape dirt road, the coast north of La Paz to San Evaristo, and over the Sierra de la Giganta.

item.title: The Making of Braelyn.ai
item.description: How a crisis of identity, a trip to Berlin, and the discovery of Berghain inspired the design of braelyn.ai.

item.title: Pacific Steel Casting
item.description: An 85-year-old steel foundry right next to I-80, empty since 2019.

item.title: Ferry Point
item.description: The end of the Santa Fe Railway, where trains used to roll onto ferries. Now it's graffiti and a rusty gantry over the bay.

item.title: Point Molate
item.description: Derelict Navy cottages at what used to be the world's largest winery.

item.title: Teufelsberg
item.description: A Cold War spy station on a hill made of Berlin's WWII rubble, now an open-air graffiti gallery.

item.title: Wünsdorf
item.description: The Soviet army's secret headquarters in East Germany, and a House of Officers with Lenin still standing out front.

item.title: Jüterbog
item.description: A secret Luftwaffe technical school, later Soviet, gone to the forest, until security found us.

item.title: Spreepark
item.description: Berlin's abandoned amusement park, twice: thrown out in ten minutes the first time, back with a plan the second, just as it was being demolished.

item.title: The Seismic Office, Treasure Island
item.description: An abandoned seismic retrofitting office on a Navy island in the middle of the bay. Went twice, the second time just after a fire. Now it’s gone.

item.title: Maharashtra and Goa on Scram 411s
item.description: Six days with Natalia on Scram 411s: Mumbai over Varandha Ghat to Mahabaleshwar, Pratapgad, Panhala, down to Goa, and back up the Konkan coast.

item.title: Rüdersdorf
item.description: A 1940s 'super cement works' turned GDR phosphate plant, abandoned since 1999. I've done it twice.

item.title: Nazi bunkers in the Calanques
item.description: German WWII bunkers and old French forts on the rocky tip of the Calanques, covered in graffiti and staring out at the Mediterranean.

item.title: Indiana Women's Prison
item.description: America's first separate prison for women, opened in 1873 and empty since 2017. Had to peep it before it was all demolished.

item.title: Lessons I've Learned As a Young, Startup Founder
item.description: Lessons learned from founding startups as a young entrepreneur. Thoughts on age, passion, pivoting, and the reality of hard work.
